claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Anthropic acquired Fractional AI in May 2026 and built Ode on it, launching with about 100 engineers and an existing client base.
claims.quote: Ode built on Fractional AI's May 2026 acquisition, launching with an existing client base and 100 engineers already in place.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Ode embeds small teams of Applied AI engineers inside customer organizations and operates Claude-first but not Claude-exclusive.
claims.quote: Ode operates Claude-first but not Claude-exclusive, allowing it to deploy rival AI models when client requirements demand it.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Ode targets community banks, regional health systems, and mid-sized manufacturers that want AI but do not employ engineers to build it.
claims.quote: The pitch is that Ode embeds small teams of Applied AI engineers inside customer organizations, works on a 'Claude-first' basis, and targets a customer segment the big labs have not really served: community banks, regional health systems, and mid-sized manufacturers that want AI but do not employ the engineers to build it.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Ode's thesis is that the moat is process rewiring, not tokens; model selection matters but is not where most effort goes.
claims.quote: Siegel's framing that 'Model selection matters, but it's not where the majority of calories are spent' is essentially the whole thesis: the moat is process rewiring, not tokens.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The TechCrunch account does not cover Ode's pricing structure, unit economics, or whether sponsor-owned portfolio customers get priority access to engineering capacity.
claims.quote: TechCrunch's account skips pricing structure, unit economics, and whether sponsor-owned portfolio customers get first pick of engineering capacity.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Ode puts Anthropic in direct commercial contact with the Deloitte and Accenture layer of enterprise IT and against OpenAI's own delivery arm.
claims.quote: First, it puts Anthropic in direct commercial contact with the Deloitte and Accenture layer of enterprise IT, and against OpenAI's own delivery arm.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Anthropic's CFO said enterprise demand for Claude is significantly outpacing any single delivery model.
claims.quote: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao framed the logic bluntly, saying 'Enterprise demand for Claude is significantly outpacing any single delivery model.'
